# Merging rubric: minimal and safe
Keep only the changes the task needs, prefer the most conservative correct version of each, and drop anything unrelated.

# Output format
You have no tools and one reply. Output ONE combined edit set built from the best parts of the candidates (you may also fix their mistakes). Copy the parts you keep in full: candidates are not applied, only your blocks are. Any prose outside code blocks is discarded.

Everything you output is applied to the ORIGINAL repository, exactly as shown to you
(line numbers in the code you were shown are display prefixes only; never copy them into
your code). Your edit set replaces any candidate edit entirely: a change you do not
re-emit will not exist in the result.

Write your edits as markdown code blocks. The first line inside each code block is a
target header starting with `@@ `; the rest of the block is the new code for that target.
Code blocks whose first line is not a header are ignored. Targets must not overlap, and
a file may not be both replaced/created/deleted as a whole and edited in parts.

Write your changes as markdown code blocks. The first line inside each code block is a header starting with `@@ ` that names the target; every following line is the body.
Each code block is one edit, and all edits must be disjoint: never target the same code twice or an element together with something inside it. Paths are relative to the project root, and every target refers to the original files you were shown, not to your other edits.

Permitted headers:
- `@@ path/to/file.py::Class.method`: replace that element (function, method or class). The body replaces the entire element, including its decorators and signature.
- `@@ path/to/file.py::Class.method::AFTER`: insert the body as a new sibling element directly after that element.
- `@@ path/to/file.py::Class.method::BEFORE`: insert the body as a new sibling element directly before that element.
- `@@ path/to/new_file.py::NEW`: create a new file whose content is the body.
- `@@ path/to/file.py::DELETE`: delete the file (the body is ignored and may be empty).
- `@@ path/to/file.py`: replace the whole file with the body.
- `@@ path/to/file.py::12-40`: replace lines 12 to 40 inclusive (line numbers of the original file) with the body.

Element paths are dotted names such as `Class.method` or `function`. The body of an element block replaces the entire element including its signature, so write the complete element. Indentation is fixed automatically.
If several elements share a dotted name (for example a property getter and its setter), append the element's first line number as shown in the code to pick one: `Class.method.12`.
Prefer element headers. Whole-file and line-span headers are discouraged: use them only when no element header fits (for example top-level code outside any element, or files that are not code).
Whole-file and line-span bodies are used verbatim: keep the exact indentation.
A whole-file, NEW or DELETE block must be the only block for its path.
Code blocks without an `@@ ` header are ignored. If a body itself contains a line of three backticks, open and close its block with four backticks (````) instead.

Example:
```python
@@ pkg/shapes.py::Circle.area
def area(self):
    return math.pi * self.radius ** 2
```

523|     def _convert_extras_requirements(self):
524|         """

526|         `"extra": ["barbazquux; {marker}"]` to
527|         `"extra:{marker}": ["barbazquux"]`.
528|         """
529|         spec_ext_reqs = getattr(self, 'extras_require', None) or {}
530|         self._tmp_extras_require = defaultdict(list)
531|         for section, v in spec_ext_reqs.items():
532|             # Do not strip empty sections.
533|             self._tmp_extras_require[section]

538|     @staticmethod

542|         that requirement.

546|     def _move_install_requirements_markers(self):
547|         """
548|         Move requirements in `install_requires` that are using environment
549|         markers `extras_require`.
550|         """
551| 
552|         # divide the install_requires into two sets, simple ones still
553|         # handled by install_requires and more complex ones handled
554|         # by extras_require.
555| 
556|         def is_simple_req(req):
557|             return not req.marker

559|         spec_inst_reqs = getattr(self, 'install_requires', None) or ()
560|         inst_reqs = list(pkg_resources.parse_requirements(spec_inst_reqs))
561|         simple_reqs = filter(is_simple_req, inst_reqs)
562|         complex_reqs = itertools.filterfalse(is_simple_req, inst_reqs)
563|         self.install_requires = list(map(str, simple_reqs))
564| 
565|         for r in complex_reqs:
566|             self._tmp_extras_require[':' + str(r.marker)].append(r)
567|         self.extras_require = dict(
568|             (k, [str(r) for r in map(self._clean_req, v)])
569|             for k, v in self._tmp_extras_require.items()

614|     def _parse_config_files(self, filenames=None):  # noqa: C901
615|         """

617|         this method provides the same functionality in subtly-improved
618|         ways.

622|         # Ignore install directory options if we have a venv
623|         ignore_options = (
624|             []
625|             if sys.prefix == sys.base_prefix
626|             else [
627|                 'install-base',
628|                 'install-platbase',
629|                 'install-lib',
630|                 'install-platlib',
631|                 'install-purelib',
632|                 'install-headers',
633|                 'install-scripts',
634|                 'install-data',
635|                 'prefix',
636|                 'exec-prefix',
637|                 'home',
638|                 'user',
639|                 'root',
640|             ]
641|         )
642| 
643|         ignore_options = frozenset(ignore_options)
644| 
645|         if filenames is None:
646|             filenames = self.find_config_files()
647| 
648|         if DEBUG:
649|             self.announce("Distribution.parse_config_files():")
650| 
651|         parser = ConfigParser()
652|         parser.optionxform = str
653|         for filename in filenames:
654|             with io.open(filename, encoding='utf-8') as reader:
655|                 if DEBUG:
656|                     self.announce("  reading {filename}".format(**locals()))
657|                 parser.read_file(reader)
658|             for section in parser.sections():
659|                 options = parser.options(section)
660|                 opt_dict = self.get_option_dict(section)
661| 
662|                 for opt in options:
663|                     if opt == '__name__' or opt in ignore_options:
664|                         continue
665| 
666|                     val = parser.get(section, opt)
667|                     opt = self.warn_dash_deprecation(opt, section)
668|                     opt = self.make_option_lowercase(opt, section)

670| 
671|             # Make the ConfigParser forget everything (so we retain
672|             # the original filenames that options come from)
673|             parser.__init__()
674| 
675|         if 'global' not in self.command_options:
676|             return
677| 
678|         # If there was a "global" section in the config file, use it
679|         # to set Distribution options.
680| 
681|         for (opt, (src, val)) in self.command_options['global'].items():
682|             alias = self.negative_opt.get(opt)
683|             if alias:
684|                 val = not strtobool(val)
685|             elif opt in ('verbose', 'dry_run'):  # ugh!
686|                 val = strtobool(val)
687| 
688|             try:
689|                 setattr(self, alias or opt, val)
690|             except ValueError as e:
691|                 raise DistutilsOptionError(e) from e

693|     def warn_dash_deprecation(self, opt, section):
694|         if section in (
695|             'options.extras_require',
696|             'options.data_files',
697|         ):
698|             return opt
699| 
700|         underscore_opt = opt.replace('-', '_')

703|             not section.startswith('options')
704|             and section != 'metadata'
705|             and section not in commands

707|             return underscore_opt

709|         if '-' in opt:
710|             warnings.warn(
711|                 "Usage of dash-separated '%s' will not be supported in future "
712|                 "versions. Please use the underscore name '%s' instead"
713|                 % (opt, underscore_opt)

1020|

1034|         contain dashes rather than underscores.  If the option doesn't take
1035|         an argument (e.g. '--quiet'), the 'val' is 'None'.
